[RARC.5.7.10] A **cache seed** ([IARC.12]) writes the
engine-owned cache directly at setup, bypassing the dispatcher. It is **not**
one of the dispatcher actions of [RARC.5.7.9]: it emits no `action_cache_set`
event. **A recording carries the seed instead,** as a `CacheSeed` in the
stream's prelude ([RFCS.26.1]), and a replay applies it before the first input
([RFCS.26.2]). So a replay starts from the cache the run started from, whether
the seed was the integrator's restore ([NSTG.9]) or a test's `initial:` arrange
([RTIM.14.4]), and the integrator does not seed the replaying engine. From
there the running cache evolves deterministically, re-derived on replay from
the cache writes the replayed rules make again ([RARC.5.7.9]) — **not** from
recorded reads or writes, neither of which a recording carries ([RFCS.3.6]).
The atom carries the value as the cache holds it, the canonical text a rule
write also produces ([IARC.12.2]), so the replayed entry is byte-identical to
the seeded one.
